decisions.reason: The accelerator program draws little on the firm's machinery engineering knowledge and yields hard-to-interpret commercial feedback, but it is still featured on the home page and costs little to keep, so it is likely retained for now despite elevated risk.

The bio-based bitumen binder sits further from the firm's mechanical plant expertise and depends on materials-science knowledge it may lack, yet its dedicated page through 2024 signals continued commitment and in-house R&D to refine it.

The WASTX Cleanic builds directly on the firm's core waste-processing machinery know-how and is strengthened by cooperation with ERMAFA, giving strong absorptive capacity to learn from results and improve the plant.
